question: does the appearance completeness contract incorrectly require EVERY injury-report row to carry Out/Doubtful/Questionable?

states.meaning: rows filed, at least one designation present
rows filed, no designation filed YET
the club has EXPLICITLY STATED it has no injury designations
states.spelled_as: nothing. There is no field in the nflverse injuries schema, no value in the report_status vocabulary, and no state in readiness.GAME_STATES that can carry it. It is therefore indistinguishable from B, and B is correctly refused.

the_real_mismatch.summary: the contract distinguishes two team states and there are three
the_real_mismatch.why_the_gate_is_right_given_its_input: C and B differ only in evidence that the injuries feed does not carry. teammate_availability is a team-level feature, so reading an unfiled designation as an absence of injury would put a fabricated availability into every vacated-share calculation for that club. The refusal is the correct behaviour for the input it has.

what_a_governance_change_would_have_to_d: whether an explicit club statement of no designations is EQUIVALENT to a filed designation for teammate_availability, or merely permits a zero-vacated-share prior
which authorities may issue such a statement, and how a later revision supersedes it
what happens when a club states no designations and a league table later shows one -- the same temporal-alignment problem already quarantined for Ajiake and Nwangwu
whether the new state is its own GAME_STATES member (auditable) or folded into READY (not auditable)

what_was_done_and_not_done.done: the explicit statements are now INGESTED and PRESERVED as their own record kind on the vintage manifest, with source hash, source url and all five clocks, under value.explicit_no_designations. They exist, hashed and clocked, instead of being discarded for want of a field.
what_was_done_and_not_done.not_done: the gate was NOT changed. No no-designation statement clears INJURY_REPORT_INCOMPLETE, and every such record carries clears_a_readiness_gate: false and the reason why.
what_was_done_and_not_done.why_not: teaching the appearance contract to accept a new CLASS of evidence changes what counts as a complete injury report. That is a governance decision reserved to the owner, not an ingestion repair, and the directive said to stop and report the mismatch rather than change governance.

test_1_executable_one_designation_in_thr.block: ZZZ, 3 rows, report_status filed on exactly 1
test_1_executable_one_designation_in_thr.conclusion: READY. The gate does NOT require every row to carry a designation; it requires at least one. The hypothesis is false.

test_2_live_a_ready_club_may_have_a_cont.conclusion: every club that cleared today did so with practice_status empty on 100% of its rows. A contract that demanded every field on every row would have cleared none of them. READY_WITH_COMPLETE_INPUT exists as a SEPARATE, stronger state precisely because "all rows, all fields" is a different claim from "this club filed a report".

falsifying_measurement.what_this_does_not_show: it does not show the gate is right about state C. It shows the gate is not wrong in the way the directive asked about.

why.the_rule_as_written: readiness.team_readiness refuses INJURY_REPORT_INCOMPLETE only when population["report_status"] == 0, i.e. when NOT ONE row on the team carries a designation. It has never required all rows to carry one.
